likely_fatal_step.why_selected_first: It is the load-bearing bridge from site-only influence to a deployable mixed W/A map. If the cost constraint is not the actual deployment peak, both allocation feasibility and the matched control can be invalid even if I_g is computed correctly.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 1. Select one publicly available DreamerV3- or TD-MPC2-style action-conditioned latent world-model checkpoint as the inferred pilot anchor and one named DeepMind Control Suite task family; freeze its FP16 weights, reproduce the native planner path, and write a reference configuration containing H_native, N_native, s_native, e_native, and the native tie rule. Inputs: public checkpoint and DMC environment. Outputs: reproducible FP16 model, planner, and configuration; no DINO-WM or LeWM backbone is introduced.
formalized_procedure.note: The native configuration is a producer for later grid/planner settings. In the original text tau is only named indirectly through the tie rule, with no numeric default or selection rule; the repaired procedure binds tau. H_native, N_native, H_episode, and M0 are method quantities, while the one-checkpoint/one-family choice is campaign scale.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 2. Trace the PyTorch scoring forward graph and enumerate G as the eligible Linear/Conv weight tensors plus their activation outputs; attach the existing uniform-affine observers without changing the FP16 path. Inputs: frozen model and planner code. Outputs: site manifest, per-site weight/activation access, and the FP16 peak-memory map; FP16 planner scores remain unchanged.
formalized_procedure.note: The original step does not say whether G is the native-path set or the union over all C cells, and FP16 no-op preservation is asserted rather than checked. A per-cell union plus a no-op score/order check is a wording repair.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 3. Build disjoint D_cal and D_eval streams from the named DMC tasks using the grid C over M, N, S, H, E, and T; for each calibration record save z_t, the FP16-generated U_t, and the cell metadata, while D_eval contains fresh environment episodes. Inputs: DMC, FP16 planner, M0 selection rule, and fixed seed manifest. Outputs: stratified calibration records and held-out episodes with no shared episode identifiers.
formalized_procedure.note: D_c is implicit and must be defined as the cell slice of D_cal. The original z_t artifact may be insufficient for a recurrent/history/cache-based scoring path, so the repaired record uses a complete replay state q_t. Empty D_c is another undefined average edge.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 4. For every g, b, and c, run site-only PTQ using the same observer data, replace only g in the FP16 checkpoint, score the identical U_t, and calculate d_g,c; the intervention propagates through every later latent transition and planner score, so its output is a changed candidate ranking and possibly a changed first action, not just a changed tensor statistic. Inputs: site manifest and D_cal. Outputs: cell-level rank-disagreement tables.
formalized_procedure.note: The original phrase normalized pairwise candidate-order disagreement has no executable pair formula, score comparator, normalization denominator, tau semantics, or K<2 behavior. Dual reading was run: R1 numeric tolerance pair signs and R2 stable total-order tie breaking give identical strict T2 values; the tie edge is reading-dependent. The mechanism remains imagined action-sequence scoring through latent transitions.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 5. Aggregate the tables into I_g,c(b) and I_g(b), retain the full profile vector across C, and compute local layer-output error and calibration-distribution fidelity only as named comparison signals. Inputs: rank-disagreement tables and omega_c. Outputs: the counterfactual influence profile and comparator table used by the allocator.
formalized_procedure.note: With D_c defined and nonempty, this is a finite-sample site-only estimator over the declared DMC/planner process. It does not estimate joint-quantization influence or a Shapley/global optimum; the candidate explicitly leaves those as empirical questions.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 6. For each M_mem in the pre-registered Pareto memory sweep, partition sites by their profile vectors and solve the stated memory-constrained assignment over B with the measured m_g and default omega_g. Inputs: I_g,c(b), m_g(b), B, omega_g, and M_mem. Outputs: a per-site weight/activation bit map; materializing that map changes which numerical operators feed future latent rollouts and therefore which action sequence the planner selects.
formalized_procedure.note: This is the likely-fatal step attacked first. The original uses sum_g m_g(b_g) while calling m_g peak-byte cost, but does not define shared-buffer/lifetime aggregation; it also says partition without a partition rule. The repaired text retains P_g as the representation and uses measured system-level PeakBytes.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 7. Materialize the all-sites mixed-precision checkpoint and run the full planner end-to-end for every c and M_mem on D_eval, allowing the selected candidate set and receding-horizon execution to follow each cell's declared convention. Inputs: FP16 checkpoint, bit map, and fresh episodes. Outputs: candidate-order agreement, first-action agreement, closed-loop return or success, peak memory, and control-frequency measurements.
formalized_procedure.note: This is the step that carries the mechanism beyond a tensor proxy: it materializes all-site quantization and runs receding-horizon control on fresh episodes. It is an evaluation protocol, not evidence that success will improve.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 8. Run matched negative controls by randomizing the mapping from I_g to bit pairs and by using the local-reconstruction allocator while preserving the same bit histogram, M_mem, candidate/update grid, receding-horizon convention, tie rule, and evaluation episodes. Inputs: the same D_eval episodes and matched resource budget. Outputs: downstream control metrics that test whether the profile, rather than resource amount alone, determines the benefit.
formalized_procedure.note: The original preserves bit histogram and target but does not require exact realized bytes; differing tensor shapes make histogram preservation insufficient. The repaired control samples only exact PeakBytes matches and records unavailable when none exists.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 9. Report the full memory-versus-control-fidelity Pareto curves and the result of the randomized mapping; choose a deployment map only by the requested M_mem target and retain all grid cells in the paper's claim, rather than selecting a favorable horizon, calibration size, planner schedule, execution convention, or tie rule after observing outcomes. Inputs: all evaluation and control tables. Outputs: an auditable method specification and falsifiable claim.
formalized_procedure.note: The no-favorable-cell selection rule is explicit. The full six-axis product is a campaign-scale quantity, not a measured runtime; the locked 12 GPU-day statement remains an estimate.

from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations

def pairwise_tol(a,b,tau):
    pairs=list(combinations(range(len(a)),2)); bad=0
    for i,j in pairs:
        sa=0 if abs(a[i]-a[j])<=tau else (1 if a[i]>a[j] else -1)
        sb=0 if abs(b[i]-b[j])<=tau else (1 if b[i]>b[j] else -1)
        bad += sa != sb
    return F(bad,len(pairs)) if pairs else None

def pairwise_stable(a,b):
    oa=sorted(range(len(a)), key=lambda i:(-a[i],i)); ob=sorted(range(len(b)), key=lambda i:(-b[i],i))
    pos_a={x:i for i,x in enumerate(oa)}; pos_b={x:i for i,x in enumerate(ob)}
    pairs=list(combinations(range(len(a)),2)); bad=0
    for i,j in pairs:
        bad += (pos_a[i] < pos_a[j]) != (pos_b[i] < pos_b[j])
    return F(bad,len(pairs)) if pairs else None

base=[F(3),F(2),F(1)]; q1=[F(6,5),F(2),F(1)]; q2=[F(3,2),F(3),F(2)]; joint=[F(6,5),F(5,2),F(12,5)]

print('reading_R2=exact_tie_stable_candidate_index', [pairwise_stable(base,q) for q in (q1,q2,joint)])

from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import combinations, product

F = Fraction

def order(scores):
    return tuple(sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: (-scores[i], i)))

def discordance(base, quant, tau=F(0)):
    pairs = list(combinations(range(len(base)), 2))
    mismatches = []
    for i, j in pairs:
        db = base[i] - base[j]
        dq = quant[i] - quant[j]
        sb = 0 if abs(db) <= tau else (1 if db > 0 else -1)
        sq = 0 if abs(dq) <= tau else (1 if dq > 0 else -1)
        mismatches.append(int(sb != sq))
    return F(sum(mismatches), len(pairs)), mismatches

def fstr(x):
    return str(x) if x.denominator != 1 else str(x.numerator)

def peak(low_sites, fp_bytes, low_bytes, shared):
    return sum(low_bytes[g] if g in low_sites else fp_bytes[g] for g in fp_bytes) + shared

# One calibration record from a two-step imagined latent action-sequence rollout.
candidates = (("a0", "a0"), ("a1", "a0"), ("a1", "a1"))
base = [F(3), F(2), F(1)]
site_scores = {
    "g1": [F(6, 5), F(2), F(1)],
    "g2": [F(3, 2), F(3), F(2)],
    "g3": [F(2), F(1), F(3)],
    "g4": base[:],
}
joint_g1g2 = [F(6, 5), F(5, 2), F(12, 5)]
rank_assignment_scores = site_scores["g1"]
naive_assignment_scores = [F(1), F(16, 5), F(5, 2)]

print("record=horizon:2,candidates=3,latent_scoring_path=imagined_action_sequences")
print("tau=0,tie_rule=stable_candidate_index")
print("baseline_scores=", [fstr(x) for x in base], "order=", order(base), "top_first_action=", candidates[order(base)[0]][0])
for g, scores in site_scores.items():
    d, mismatches = discordance(base, scores)
    print("single", g, "scores=", [fstr(x) for x in scores], "order=", order(scores), "pair_mismatches=", mismatches, "d=", fstr(d))
d_joint, joint_mismatches = discordance(base, joint_g1g2)
print("joint_g1_g2 scores=", [fstr(x) for x in joint_g1g2], "order=", order(joint_g1g2), "pair_mismatches=", joint_mismatches, "d=", fstr(d_joint))
d1 = discordance(base, site_scores["g1"])[0]
d2 = discordance(base, site_scores["g2"])[0]
print("interaction_check=d_joint-(d_g1+d_g2)=", fstr(d_joint - d1 - d2), "d_joint=", fstr(d_joint), "sum_single=", fstr(d1+d2))

# Full declared six-axis grid, with small concrete parameters.
grid = {
    "H": sorted({4 // 2, 4, min(2 * 4, 6)}),
    "N": sorted({max(1, 4 // 2), 4, 2 * 4}),
    "M": sorted({max(1, 4 // 4), max(1, 4 // 2), 4}),
    "S": ("native", "random_shooting", "CEM"),
    "E": ("native", "one_step"),
    "T": ("stable_index", "seeded_random"),
}
raw_cells = list(product(*(grid[k] for k in ("H", "N", "M", "S", "E", "T"))))
print("grid_axes=", {k: list(v) for k, v in grid.items()})
print("grid_cells_raw=", len(raw_cells), "grid_cells_after_dedup=", len(set(raw_cells)), "full_grid_omega_c=", fstr(F(1, len(set(raw_cells)))))
print("trace_cell_count=1,trace_cell_omega_c=1")

# Four sites with unequal resident weights and one shared peak workspace.
fp_bytes = {"g1": 12, "g2": 8, "g3": 8, "g4": 4}
low_bytes = {g: v // 4 for g, v in fp_bytes.items()}
shared_workspace = 4
site_peak = {"FP16": {g: fp_bytes[g] + shared_workspace for g in fp_bytes},
             "W4A4": {g: low_bytes[g] + shared_workspace for g in fp_bytes}}
rank_low = {"g1", "g4"}
naive_low = {"g2", "g3"}
bad_perm_low = {"g1", "g2"}
print("bytes_fp=", fp_bytes, "bytes_w4a4=", low_bytes, "shared_workspace=", shared_workspace)
rank_sum = sum(site_peak["W4A4"][g] if g in rank_low else site_peak["FP16"][g] for g in fp_bytes)
naive_sum = sum(site_peak["W4A4"][g] if g in naive_low else site_peak["FP16"][g] for g in fp_bytes)
rank_peak = peak(rank_low, fp_bytes, low_bytes, shared_workspace)
naive_peak = peak(naive_low, fp_bytes, low_bytes, shared_workspace)
print("rank_assignment_low=", sorted(rank_low), "sum_individual_m=", rank_sum, "actual_peak=", rank_peak)
print("naive_assignment_low=", sorted(naive_low), "sum_individual_m=", naive_sum, "actual_peak=", naive_peak)
print("bad_permutation_low=", sorted(bad_perm_low), "same_bit_histogram=True", "actual_peak=", peak(bad_perm_low, fp_bytes, low_bytes, shared_workspace), "same_as_rank_peak=", peak(bad_perm_low, fp_bytes, low_bytes, shared_workspace) == rank_peak)
print("matched_nontrivial_permutation=", sorted(naive_low), "same_bit_histogram=True", "same_peak=", naive_peak == rank_peak)
print("minimum_all_low_peak=", peak(set(fp_bytes), fp_bytes, low_bytes, shared_workspace))

local_error = {"g1": F(20, 100), "g2": F(5, 100), "g3": F(8, 100), "g4": F(30, 100)}
influence = {g: discordance(base, site_scores[g])[0] for g in site_scores}
rank_raw = sum(influence[g] for g in rank_low)
naive_raw = sum(influence[g] for g in naive_low)
print("influence_profile=", {g: fstr(influence[g]) for g in influence}, "omega_g=", fstr(F(1, 4)))
print("local_reconstruction_error=", {g: fstr(local_error[g]) for g in local_error}, "naive_low_sites=smallest_error=", sorted(naive_low))
print("weighted_allocator_objective_rankcal=", fstr(rank_raw / 4), "raw_sum=", fstr(rank_raw), "weighted_allocator_objective_naive_map=", fstr(naive_raw / 4), "raw_sum=", fstr(naive_raw), "M_mem=24")
d_rank, _ = discordance(base, rank_assignment_scores)
d_naive, _ = discordance(base, naive_assignment_scores)
print("rankcal_downstream_order=", order(rank_assignment_scores), "d=", fstr(d_rank), "rank_agreement=", fstr(1-d_rank), "first_action=", candidates[order(rank_assignment_scores)[0]][0])
print("naive_downstream_order=", order(naive_assignment_scores), "d=", fstr(d_naive), "rank_agreement=", fstr(1-d_naive), "first_action=", candidates[order(naive_assignment_scores)[0]][0])
print("t5_divergence_d_naive_minus_rankcal=", fstr(d_naive-d_rank), "kind=instance_contingent")
print("declared_gpu_days=12,measurement_status=unmeasured_estimate")

The central object is the rollout-ranking influence profile I_g,c(b)=average_r in D_c of d_g,c(r;b) and I_g(b)=sum_c omega_c I_g,c(b), a dimensionless counterfactual estimand of how much site g changes planner ordering over the observed rollout regime; finite accumulators compute the stated finite-sample estimator, subject to ordinary numerical rounding, rather than approximating an unchosen Shapley value. The heterogeneous companion retains each full profile vector P_g=(I_g,c(b)) across cells as its heterogeneity representation (no unbound clustering rule) and chooses b_g by minimizing sum_g omega_g I_g(b_g) subject to the system-level PeakBytes(b_1,...,b_|G|) <= M_mem, where PeakBytes is measured on the materialized end-to-end graph and includes resident weights, activation lifetimes and shared tensors, scales/zero-points, weight copies, and backend workspace; m_g(b) remains a diagnostic per-site record, not a quantity to sum as though sites were disjoint. The resulting all-sites assignment is evaluated end-to-end on disjoint episodes for every feasible grid cell and memory target, reporting rank agreement, first-action agreement, closed-loop return or success, peak memory, and control frequency; the influence profile is therefore an empirical allocation signal rather than a claim of global optimality. applied_revisions.value:
1. Select one publicly available DreamerV3- or TD-MPC2-style action-conditioned latent world-model checkpoint as the inferred pilot anchor and one named DeepMind Control Suite task family; freeze its FP16 weights, reproduce the native planner path, and write a reference configuration containing H_native, N_native, s_native, e_native, and the native tie rule. Bind tau=0 by default (exact score equality) with stable candidate-index resolution for ties; any nonzero tolerance must be preregistered before D_cal. Inputs: public checkpoint and DMC environment. Outputs: reproducible FP16 model, planner, and configuration; no DINO-WM or LeWM backbone is introduced.
2. Trace the PyTorch scoring forward graph over every declared grid cell and enumerate G as the deterministic union of the eligible Linear/Conv weight tensors W_g plus activation outputs A_g; require |G| >= 1. Attach the existing uniform-affine observers without changing the FP16 path, and reject the manifest if the observer attachment changes any FP16 planner score or candidate order. Inputs: frozen model, planner code, and declared grid. Outputs: site manifest, per-site weight/activation access, and the FP16 memory accounting record; FP16 planner scores remain unchanged only after this no-op check passes.
3. Build disjoint D_cal and D_eval streams from the named DMC tasks using the grid C over M, N, S, H, E, and T; define D_c={r in D_cal: cell(r)=c}. For each calibration record save the complete planner replay state q_t=(z_t plus any recurrent/history/cache/normalization/RNG state needed for replay), the FP16-generated U_t, and cell metadata, while D_eval contains fresh environment episodes with no shared episode identifiers. Require each evaluated D_c to be nonempty; otherwise mark the cell unavailable rather than forming a zero-denominator mean. Inputs: DMC, FP16 planner, M0 selection rule, and fixed seed manifest. Outputs: stratified calibration records and held-out episodes.
4. For every g, b, and c, run site-only PTQ using the same observer data, replace only g in the FP16 checkpoint, and score the identical U_t through the declared imagined latent rollout. Let K_r=|U_t|; for K_r >= 2 set d_g,c(r;b)=[sum_{i<j} 1{ord_tau(s_g,b(u_i),s_g,b(u_j)) != ord_tau(s_FP16(u_i),s_FP16(u_j))}]/binom(K_r,2), where ord_tau treats scores within tau as a tie and resolves it by candidate index; for K_r < 2 set d_g,c(r;b)=0 and record the zero-pair count. The intervention propagates through every later latent transition and planner score, so its output is a changed candidate ranking and possibly a changed first action, not just a changed tensor statistic. Inputs: site manifest and D_cal. Outputs: cell-level rank-disagreement tables.
5. Aggregate the tables into I_g,c(b) and I_g(b), retain the full profile vector across C, and compute local layer-output error and calibration-distribution fidelity only as named comparison signals. Inputs: rank-disagreement tables and omega_c. Outputs: the finite-sample counterfactual influence profile and comparator table used by the allocator.
6. For each feasible M_mem in the pre-registered Pareto memory sweep, retain the full profile vector as the heterogeneity representation and solve the stated memory-constrained assignment over B_deploy with the measured system-level PeakBytes(b_1,...,b_|G|) <= M_mem; if no assignment is feasible, mark that cell/target infeasible and report no downstream metric rather than silently substituting another map. Inputs: I_g,c(b), PeakBytes, B_deploy, omega_g, and M_mem. Outputs: a per-site weight/activation bit map; materializing that map changes which numerical operators feed future latent rollouts and therefore which action sequence the planner selects.
7. Materialize the all-sites mixed-precision checkpoint and run the full planner end-to-end for every feasible c and M_mem on D_eval, allowing the selected candidate set and receding-horizon execution to follow each cell's declared convention. Inputs: FP16 checkpoint, bit map, and fresh episodes. Outputs: candidate-order agreement, first-action agreement, closed-loop return or success, peak memory, and control-frequency measurements.
8. Run matched negative controls by sampling non-identity assignments with the same bit-pair histogram and exact measured PeakBytes as the RankCal assignment, and by using the local-reconstruction allocator while preserving the same M_mem, candidate/update grid, receding-horizon convention, tie rule, planner seeds, and evaluation episodes. If no non-identity assignment satisfies both matches, record the control as unavailable; interpret an observed difference as a matched diagnostic, not a proof that I_g is the sole causal factor. Inputs: the same D_eval episodes and matched resource budget. Outputs: downstream control metrics that test whether the profile, rather than resource amount alone, determines the benefit.
9. Report the full memory-versus-control-fidelity Pareto curves and the result of the randomized mapping; choose a deployment map only by the requested feasible M_mem target and retain all feasible grid cells in the paper's claim, rather than selecting a favorable horizon, calibration size, planner schedule, execution convention, or tie rule after observing outcomes. Inputs: all evaluation and control tables. Outputs: an auditable method specification and falsifiable claim.
applied_revisions.delta_summary: Repairs T1/T3 findings by binding tau and M0, defining the pairwise estimator and K<2 behavior, recording complete planner state and D_c, checking FP16 no-op behavior, clamping H, handling empty/infeasible cells, and enforcing exact histogram-plus-PeakBytes controls.

final_candidate.title: RankCal: Counterfactual Influence Quantization for Action-Conditioned Latent World-Model Planning
final_candidate.hook: At matched memory and nominal bit-width, candidate-order agreement should improve more by protecting sites with high rollout-ranking influence than by protecting sites with the largest local reconstruction error, especially in the longer-horizon cells of the evaluation grid. This predicts that a deliberately worse tensor-MSE allocation can yield higher closed-loop success, exposing a decision-level failure mode that the full-text DINO-WM sweep did not measure.
final_candidate.hook_shape_rationale: I choose (a) because the primary metric is downstream candidate-order agreement and closed-loop success, and the surprising direction is that influence-guided precision can outperform local-MSE precision even when its tensor reconstruction is worse; the full-text DINO-WM record reports module, granularity, and horizon effects but not this causal ranking comparison. Shape (b) was viable as motivation, but I reject it because merely renaming local PTQ fidelity as a tacit assumption would not construct the computable influence profile or predict a downstream direction.

gap_closure.gap: For the setting studied by arxiv:2602.02110v1, and more generally for action-conditioned latent world models, no retrieved leaf establishes whether a low-bit perturbation preserves the ranking of candidate action sequences as the imagined-rollout horizon and visited latent states change — stakes: practitioners can deploy a model that looks acceptable on local or short-horizon metrics but selects systematically worse actions, wasting the single-GPU pilot and blocking reliable closed-loop control; intellectually, PTQ conclusions do not transfer from visual-goal planning to model-based control.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by reframing multi-step ranking preservation as a fixed-model counterfactual influence score over identical planner candidates, then partitioning sites by the resulting profile and solving a memory-constrained heterogeneous weight/activation bit assignment; corpus support is thin in world-model quantization, with the closest C00 exemplars coming from fixed-model attribution and uncertainty measurement.

final_candidate.core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger
P1. Candidate action-sequence ordering is the operational decision variable, not merely a proxy for latent or observation reconstruction — reason: the planner selects actions by comparing candidate scores.
P2. A site-only quantization intervention with the candidate pool, FP16 weights elsewhere, and planner inputs held fixed isolates a useful marginal decision influence (untested — falsification target) — reason: it creates a matched counterfactual while preserving the downstream scoring path.
P3. The influence profile transfers sufficiently from FP16 planner visitation to quantized receding-horizon visitation for allocation to help (untested — falsification target) — reason: the calibration stream is generated by the same control loop, but low-bit errors can move later states off that stream.
P4. Site-level marginal influence is sufficiently compositional for a memory-constrained assignment to be useful even though joint quantization can interact (untested — falsification target) — reason: the single-site table makes the pilot tractable, while the all-sites evaluation tests the approximation.
P5. Existing public weights expose the eligible weight tensors and activation outputs needed for numerical PTQ, and the chosen DMC model/planner path can be run at FP16 and mixed W/A precision — reason: the proposal uses model-internal access, not gradients, closed-model APIs, or a new training corpus.
OBSERVATION-MODEL: D_cal is sampled as stratified trajectories from named DMC tasks under the FP16 native, random-shooting, and CEM schedules, with fixed start-state and random-seed manifests; it is not unbiased over all reachable latent states, is biased toward the FP16 planner's visitation and candidate distribution, and is kept disjoint from D_eval.
ESTIMAND: for each site g and bit pair b, I_g(b) estimates the expected normalized pairwise candidate-order discordance between the FP16 planner and the model with only g quantized, over the uniform-weighted cells C and the records D_c drawn from this stated DMC/planner process; it is conditional on that process, not an unbiased population average over all states, tasks, or backbones.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
Naive version: run uniform-affine PTQ, select each site's weight and activation bits by lowest layer-output reconstruction error on short calibration trajectories, and spend the remaining memory budget on the sites with the smallest local error.
It fails under branch (i): this version silently assumes that local reconstruction and calibration-distribution fidelity predict candidate ranking under recurrent action-conditioned rollouts, a premise that is false as a general rule because planner-induced states and candidate orderings change with horizon. RankCal confronts that failure with site-only counterfactual ranking influence; although counterfactual intervention is a standard diagnostic tool, the domain-specific structure is the adaptive candidate pool plus receding-horizon latent feedback under a fixed mixed W/A memory budget, so this is an application-grade method rather than a claim of a new generic causal estimator.
BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE
I kept one anchor and deferred the cross-backbone transfer gap and the standalone local-proxy audit because the former is a validation axis and the latter is a negative-control comparison that can run through the same anchor machinery; adding either as a separate leg would make the paper broader without making the method more complete.
I selected C00 from the anchor alternates because its fixed-model counterfactual measurement object directly matches candidate-order influence, while the heterogeneous companion turns that object into a runnable memory-constrained W/A allocation.
The method's central object is defined as a site-isolated estimand and the final full-model evaluation, not a claimed Shapley or globally additive optimum; this keeps the C00 compression step honest when joint quantization interactions violate additivity.
I rejected uniform local-reconstruction, generic activation-sensitivity, and module/horizon-only routes because they regress to the established n0-n2 PTQ lineage or repeat the n3 DINO-WM sweep; DINO-WM and LeFlow are full-text comparators, QuantWAMs is connector-verified but abstract-only and adjacent, and DreamerV3/TD-MPC2 remain explicitly inferred pilot anchors.
final_candidate.core_mechanism_steps:
1. Select one publicly available DreamerV3- or TD-MPC2-style action-conditioned latent world-model checkpoint as the inferred pilot anchor and one named DeepMind Control Suite task family; freeze its FP16 weights, reproduce the native planner path, and write a reference configuration containing H_native, N_native, s_native, e_native, and the native tie rule. Bind tau=0 by default (exact score equality) with stable candidate-index resolution for ties; any nonzero tolerance must be preregistered before D_cal. Inputs: public checkpoint and DMC environment. Outputs: reproducible FP16 model, planner, and configuration; no DINO-WM or LeWM backbone is introduced.
2. Trace the PyTorch scoring forward graph over every declared grid cell and enumerate G as the deterministic union of the eligible Linear/Conv weight tensors W_g plus activation outputs A_g; require |G| >= 1. Attach the existing uniform-affine observers without changing the FP16 path, and reject the manifest if the observer attachment changes any FP16 planner score or candidate order. Inputs: frozen model, planner code, and declared grid. Outputs: site manifest, per-site weight/activation access, and the FP16 memory accounting record; FP16 planner scores remain unchanged only after this no-op check passes.
3. Build disjoint D_cal and D_eval streams from the named DMC tasks using the grid C over M, N, S, H, E, and T; define D_c={r in D_cal: cell(r)=c}. For each calibration record save the complete planner replay state q_t=(z_t plus any recurrent/history/cache/normalization/RNG state needed for replay), the FP16-generated U_t, and cell metadata, while D_eval contains fresh environment episodes with no shared episode identifiers. Require each evaluated D_c to be nonempty; otherwise mark the cell unavailable rather than forming a zero-denominator mean. Inputs: DMC, FP16 planner, M0 selection rule, and fixed seed manifest. Outputs: stratified calibration records and held-out episodes.
4. For every g, b, and c, run site-only PTQ using the same observer data, replace only g in the FP16 checkpoint, and score the identical U_t through the declared imagined latent rollout. Let K_r=|U_t|; for K_r >= 2 set d_g,c(r;b)=[sum_{i<j} 1{ord_tau(s_g,b(u_i),s_g,b(u_j)) != ord_tau(s_FP16(u_i),s_FP16(u_j))}]/binom(K_r,2), where ord_tau treats scores within tau as a tie and resolves it by candidate index; for K_r < 2 set d_g,c(r;b)=0 and record the zero-pair count. The intervention propagates through every later latent transition and planner score, so its output is a changed candidate ranking and possibly a changed first action, not just a changed tensor statistic. Inputs: site manifest and D_cal. Outputs: cell-level rank-disagreement tables.
5. Aggregate the tables into I_g,c(b) and I_g(b), retain the full profile vector across C, and compute local layer-output error and calibration-distribution fidelity only as named comparison signals. Inputs: rank-disagreement tables and omega_c. Outputs: the finite-sample counterfactual influence profile and comparator table used by the allocator.
6. For each feasible M_mem in the pre-registered Pareto memory sweep, retain the full profile vector as the heterogeneity representation and solve the stated memory-constrained assignment over B_deploy with the measured system-level PeakBytes(b_1,...,b_|G|) <= M_mem; if no assignment is feasible, mark that cell/target infeasible and report no downstream metric rather than silently substituting another map. Inputs: I_g,c(b), PeakBytes, B_deploy, omega_g, and M_mem. Outputs: a per-site weight/activation bit map; materializing that map changes which numerical operators feed future latent rollouts and therefore which action sequence the planner selects.
7. Materialize the all-sites mixed-precision checkpoint and run the full planner end-to-end for every feasible c and M_mem on D_eval, allowing the selected candidate set and receding-horizon execution to follow each cell's declared convention. Inputs: FP16 checkpoint, bit map, and fresh episodes. Outputs: candidate-order agreement, first-action agreement, closed-loop return or success, peak memory, and control-frequency measurements.
8. Run matched negative controls by sampling non-identity assignments with the same bit-pair histogram and exact measured PeakBytes as the RankCal assignment, and by using the local-reconstruction allocator while preserving the same M_mem, candidate/update grid, receding-horizon convention, tie rule, planner seeds, and evaluation episodes. If no non-identity assignment satisfies both matches, record the control as unavailable; interpret an observed difference as a matched diagnostic, not a proof that I_g is the sole causal factor. Inputs: the same D_eval episodes and matched resource budget. Outputs: downstream control metrics that test whether the profile, rather than resource amount alone, determines the benefit.
9. Report the full memory-versus-control-fidelity Pareto curves and the result of the randomized mapping; choose a deployment map only by the requested feasible M_mem target and retain all feasible grid cells in the paper's claim, rather than selecting a favorable horizon, calibration size, planner schedule, execution convention, or tie rule after observing outcomes. Inputs: all evaluation and control tables. Outputs: an auditable method specification and falsifiable claim.
final_candidate.falsification_prediction: Minimal experiment: on one public FP16 DreamerV3- or TD-MPC2-style checkpoint (inferred pilot anchor) and one DeepMind Control Suite visual continuous-control task, compare RankCal with uniform-bit and local-reconstruction allocation at matched peak memory across the full C grid. If the mechanism works, the primary downstream metric, closed-loop task-success rate, will be higher for RankCal than for the matched controls, while candidate-order and first-action agreement will degrade less in the longer-horizon cells. The single load-bearing variable is I_g(b), the site-only rollout-ranking influence profile; randomize its mapping to bit pairs while preserving the bit histogram, memory, candidate/update schedule, receding-horizon convention, and tie rule, then rerun fresh D_eval episodes. The negative control predicts that the randomized map's downstream task-success rate returns to the matched local-reconstruction or uniform-PTQ baseline, not merely that I_g changes; if the benefit survives the randomized mapping, the proposed influence signal is not the mechanism carrying the result.
final_candidate.compute_budget: GPU: estimated 12 GPU-days on one NSCC ASPIRE2A A100-SXM4-40GB for the one-task pilot, site-only probes, full nuisance grid, matched controls, and held-out closed-loop evaluation; an optional second DMC task family would add an estimated 6 GPU-days. API: $0 for the full campaign because model inference, calibration, and evaluation are local and no paid API judge is required. No GPU experiments are run during this proposal phase.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: The full-text-backed DINO-WM record constructs a systematic weight-only and joint weight-activation PTQ sweep over methods, granularity, modules, and planning horizons, whereas RankCal constructs a site-level counterfactual candidate-order influence profile over action-conditioned latent states and uses it for memory-constrained mixed W/A assignment.

The full-text-backed LeFlow record replaces repeated CEM search with rectified-flow latent trajectory generation, inverse-dynamics decoding, and frozen-LeWM rollout reranking, whereas RankCal leaves the planner and latent backbone fixed and changes the numerical PTQ calibration/allocation signal to preserve candidate ordering under multi-step quantized rollouts.

The connector-verified but abstract-only adjacent QuantWAMs record proposes coordinate-compatible activation evidence, joint video-action saliency, and fixed-intervention auditing for WAM PTQ, whereas RankCal targets latent-dynamics planner rankings without WAM future/action coupling and derives weight/activation bits from site-only ranking influence.

final_candidate.what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to hold candidate pools, planner inputs, receding-horizon conventions, and tie rules fixed while quantizing one site at a time, estimate that site's candidate-order discordance over action-conditioned rollout states, and solve the resulting profile as a memory-constrained mixed W/A assignment; the supplied method constructs PTQ sweeps and outcome analyses but not this decision-influence object or allocation step.
